title: Woolly Aphids on Crepe Myrtle in Baton Rouge
seo_title: Woolly Aphids on Crepe Myrtle in Baton Rouge | Grow Green
seo_desc: Woolly aphids left sticky honeydew and black sooty mold on a Burbank-area crepe myrtle. See how tree and shrub care helped the tree improve.

faqs.q: Are woolly aphids the same as white fungus on the trunk?
faqs.a: No. The white, cottony look is usually the insect’s waxy covering. Black sooty mold is a separate fungus that grows on honeydew the aphids produce.

faqs.q: Will scrubbing black sooty mold fix the tree?
faqs.a: Cleaning may temporarily improve appearance, but sooty mold typically returns if aphids keep producing honeydew. Addressing the aphids is the lasting step; mold then fades over time.

faqs.q: Do crepe myrtles in Baton Rouge get woolly aphids often?
faqs.a: Crepe myrtles are common landscape trees here, and soft-bodied pests such as aphids show up regularly during the growing season — especially when new growth and warm weather line up.

faqs.q: Is tree and shrub care only for aphids?
faqs.a: No. The program covers seasonal monitoring and management for ornamental pests and disease pressure, plus nutrition support when appropriate — aphids are one of several issues we watch for.

faqs.q: How fast does sooty mold disappear after treatment?
faqs.a: It varies. Once honeydew stops, existing mold usually weathers away gradually rather than disappearing the same week as treatment.
